stops.name: Rouen, Margaret invoked one hundred and twenty-eight times
stops.campa: Across the record of Rouen's trial, the name Margaret is invoked one hundred and twenty-eight times, more than any other word save God and the king, as Jehanne answers question after question about the voice that speaks the tongue of France, beautiful, sweet and low, and will not, asked directly, speak English, for she is not on the English side. The judges who count every heresy do not count how often they themselves say the name trying to trap her with it. Margaret, examined by proxy through her servant's mouth for eighty-nine days, never once appears in the court to answer for herself.

stops.name: Obernburg am Main, the Anna-Kapelle, and the three holy maids
stops.campa: On the Nothelferaltar of the little Anna-Kapelle at Obernburg am Main, some fifty kilometers up the river from Frankfurt, a carved verse fixes the three virgin martyrs together for good, past every timeline, past every twin name: Margaretha mit dem Wurm, Barbara mit dem Turm, Katharina mit dem Radl: Margaret with the dragon, Barbara with the tower, Catherine with the wheel, das sind die drei heiligen Madl, those are the three holy maids. The chapel keeps no record of Thecla, Pelagia, or Marina by name, only the dragon-image that carries all their weight at once: the last water this life is seen through, a plaque instead of a voice.
stops.quote: Margaretha mit dem Wurm, Barbara mit dem Turm, Katharina mit dem Radl, das sind die drei heiligen Madl.
stops.quote_source: Nothelferaltar inscription, Annakapelle, Obernburg am Main (late 18th c.); essays/213_las_tres_virgenes_martires.md
